brief.headline: This supplier is in the distress zone and losing money — lead with supply security and line up a second source, but DO offer to pay faster (they need cash) for a modest price cut around 2.77%.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹1.62/NOS on the LDPE bottle (matching our cheapest supplier) plus a 2–3% cut across the board to reflect their reseller margin and our faster payment.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.62/NOS for LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE, saving roughly ₹3.37 L/year; a further 2.77% cut if we pay 15 days faster
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹1.62/NOS to Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited for the same bottle; Berry's ₹1.69/NOS is 4.3% higher. They are 100.0% a trader, so their price carries a reseller margin. Paying them 15 days faster is worth about 2.77% to them (their borrowing rate), so a matching price cut is fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep our current 30 days — do NOT offer more credit (they're fragile). Instead, offer to pay 15 days earlier (in 15 days) in exchange for the 2.77% price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier ties up an extra ₹3.34 L of our cash, but the 2.77% price cut (roughly ₹2.25 L/year on ₹81.39 L spend) makes it close to neutral for us and frees up cash for them.

brief.financialLeverage: Berry is in serious trouble: they lost ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24, keep -199.2% of every rupee they sell (vs 2.3% for similar firms), owe 220.44 times their own cash, and sit in the distress zone (score -0.18). Their cash is stuck for 335 days (vs 70 for peers), so they desperately need faster payment. We are 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr revenue — a big customer — but pushing too hard on price could tip them over and kill our supply. The play: offer faster payment (which they value highly) for a modest price cut, frame it as a partnership to keep them stable, and quietly qualify Manjushree Technopack (₹2569.83 Cr, score B 65/100) as our backup so we're covered if Berry folds.

evidence.point: They keep far less profit than similar firms
Their cash is stuck much longer than peers
We are a big customer to them
They owe a huge amount relative to their own cash
We pay more to them than to our cheapest supplier for the same bottle

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100), makes pharma bottles and caps — the strongest alternate to qualify now.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable, a robust second source for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — direct fit if we use PET bottles.

risks: Berry is in the distress zone (score -0.18) and lost ₹-22.50 Cr last year — real risk they fold or cut quality to survive. Do not increase our spend with them; get a second source audited fast.
They are 100.0% a trader (not a maker), so if their own supplier raises prices or cuts them off, we have no fallback and Berry has no room to absorb it.
Their overall money-health score is 1/10 — the weakest possible. Any shock (late customer payment, bank pressure) could stop our supply overnight.
Pushing a big price cut now could push them into bankruptcy, leaving us scrambling. The 2.77% ask tied to faster payment is the safe limit.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and want to keep it stable — we're ready to pay you 15 days faster to help your cash flow, and in return we'd like you to match the ₹1.62/NOS we pay elsewhere and take another 2–3% off to reflect that faster payment.
